title: The Connectome: Mapping Every Wire
summary: A connectome is the complete wiring diagram of a nervous system.
body:
Postbiological cognition studies minds beyond biology: whole-brain emulation, neuromorphic hardware, and the theories that would tell us whether an upload is conscious. Real neuroscience, real philosophy, open questions.

A connectome is the complete wiring diagram of a nervous system. C. elegans (302 neurons) was fully mapped in 1986; the fruit fly brain (140,000 neurons) followed in 2024. The human brain's 86 billion neurons remain far beyond full mapping.

title: Whole Brain Emulation: The Proposal
summary: Whole brain emulation (WBE) would scan a brain at sufficient resolution and simulate it.
body:
Whole brain emulation (WBE) would scan a brain at sufficient resolution and simulate it. Anders Sandberg's 2008 roadmap estimated the computational and scanning requirements; the concept drives both hope and fierce philosophical debate.

title: Simulating a Neuron Faithfully
summary: How much detail must a simulation capture? Hodgkin-Huxley equations model ion channels; simpler integrate-and-fire models suffice for many network behaviors.
body:
How much detail must a simulation capture? Hodgkin-Huxley equations model ion channels; simpler integrate-and-fire models suffice for many network behaviors. The emulation debate hinges on which level preserves the mind.

Context: this record is part of the Postbiological Cognition catalog — postbiological cognition studies minds beyond biology: whole-brain emulation, neuromorphic hardware, and the theories that would tell us whether an upload is conscious.
facts: Blue Brain modeled a cortical column (2015)

program.code:
# Leaky integrate-and-fire neuron: the workhorse model
import math
def simulate_neuron(I=1.5, tau=20.0, v_th=1.0, dt=0.1, t_max=200.0):
    v, spikes, t = 0.0, [], 0.0
    while t < t_max:
        v += dt*(-v/tau + I/tau)
        if v >= v_th:
            spikes.append(t); v = 0.0
        t += dt
    return spikes
sp = simulate_neuron()
print(f"spikes: {len(sp)}, rate: {len(sp)/0.2:.1f} Hz")
